subject: English
question_text: Why didn't he pay the school fees on the day he brought money to school?
answer_text: He did not pay the school fees on the day he brought money to school because Master Ghulam Mohammed (the teacher who collected the fees) was on leave, and it would be collected the next day.
final_answer: Therefore, he did not pay the fees as the teacher was absent.

subject: English
question_text: What were the coins 'saying' to him? Do you think they were misguiding him?

parts.part_text: What were the coins 'saying' to him?
parts.answer_text: The coins were asking him to buy the jalebis. They said that those fresh, hot jalebis were not coming out for nothing. Jalebis were meant to be eaten, and only those with money in their pocket could eat them. They also said that money was meant to be spent, and only those who liked jalebis spent it.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the coins urged him to spend his money on jalebis.

parts.part_text: Do you think they were misguiding him?
parts.answer_text: Yes, they were misguiding him. Even though the money was for the payment of fees, they urged him to spend all on jalebis.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, the coins misled him regarding his priorities.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the character's conflict and motivations.

subject: English
question_text: Why didn't he take the coins' advice? Give two or three reasons.

parts.part_text: Why didn't he take the coins' advice?
parts.answer_text: He did not take the coins' advice because he was a good boy. He knew that the coins were misguiding him.
parts.final_answer: Thus, he chose to ignore their temptation.

parts.answer_text: He said he got so much at home that he considered even looking at something in the market a sin. Besides, the coins were his fees. If he spent them that day, he would not be able to show his face to Master Ghulam Mohammed the next day at school, and after that to God.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, he felt a strong moral obligation to save the money for his fees.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding character motivations and moral reasoning.

subject: English
question_text: What did the oldest coin tell him? Did he follow his advice? If not, why not?

parts.part_text: What did the oldest coin tell him?
parts.answer_text: The oldest coin said that they were trying to tell him something for his own good. It said that he would get the scholarship money the next day, and with that money he could pay his fees. Hence, he could very well buy the jalebis with the fees money.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the coin encouraged him to spend the fees money on jalebis.

parts.part_text: Did he follow his advice? If not, why not?
parts.answer_text: No, he did not follow its advice. Even though his mouth watered, he remembered the fact that he was among the most promising students at school. He had never once been beaten. He thought that for a child of such status, standing in the middle of the market and eating jalebis was inappropriate.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, he chose to uphold his reputation and values over temptation.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of character values and decision-making.

subject: English
question_text: He reached home with the coins in his pocket. What happened then?
answer_text: When he reached home, the coins began to speak again. When he went inside to have lunch, they began to shriek. He was so thoroughly fed up that he rushed out of the house barefoot and ran towards the market.
final_answer: Thus, he succumbed to the temptation of jalebis.

subject: English
question_text: Why didn't he eat all the jalebis he had bought? What did he do with the remaining jalebis?

parts.part_text: Why didn't he eat all the jalebis he had bought?
parts.answer_text: He did not eat all the jalebis he had bought because he had eaten so many of them that if anybody pressed his stomach a little, jalebis would have popped out of his ears and nostrils.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, he was too full to eat more.

parts.part_text: What did he do with the remaining jalebis?
parts.answer_text: He distributed the remaining jalebis to the children who had assembled in the gali where he was eating the jalebis.
parts.final_answer: Thus, he shared his excess jalebis with others.

subject: English
question_text: "The fear was killing me." What was the fear?
answer_text: The fear was of getting caught and his parents finding out that he had eaten so many jalebis. He burped with every breath. With every burp, there was the danger of bringing out a jalebi or two.
final_answer: Thus, he was terrified of the consequences of his actions.

subject: English
question_text: When it is time to pay the fees, what does he do? How is he disobeying the elders by doing so?
answer_text: When it was time to pay the fees, he tucked his bag under his arm and left the school. He kept walking, praying for some miracle to happen which would save him that one time. He reached the Kambelpur railway station. The elders had warned him to never cross the railway tracks. They had also warned him that one must never eat sweets with one's fees money. However, he had disobeyed them by doing so.
final_answer: Thus, he ignored the warnings of his elders.

subject: English
question_text: Discuss the following points. Is the boy intelligent? If so, what is the evidence of it? Does his outlook on the jalebis episode change after class VIII? Does he see that episode in a new light? Why are coins made to 'talk' in this story? What purpose does it serve?

parts.part_text: Is the boy intelligent? If so, what is the evidence of it?
parts.answer_text: Yes, the boy was intelligent. In school, he was among the most promising students. In his fourth standard exam, he had won a scholarship of four rupees a month. He was also going to get the previous month's scholarship on the day he had to pay his fees. Also, he had never been absent from school.
parts.final_answer: Thus, his academic achievements indicate his intelligence.

parts.part_text: Does his outlook on the jalebis episode change after class VIII? Does he see that episode in a new light?
parts.answer_text: Up to class VIII, he kept wondering what harm it could have possibly caused anyone if God had sent him four rupees that day. However, later, he came to the conclusion that if God were to provide all for the asking, then man would still be living in nests such as vultures and crows, and would not have learnt the art of making jalebis.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, he realizes the importance of effort and hard work.

parts.part_text: Why are coins made to 'talk' in this story? What purpose does it serve?
parts.answer_text: Coins are made to 'talk' in the story to show the greedy nature of the boy. His good nature, which prevented him from spending money on jalebis, comes out in the form of the words spoken by him. His greed, which was pushing him to get the jalebis and devour them, is brought out in the words uttered by the coins.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the talking coins symbolize his internal conflict between greed and morality.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves critical thinking and analysis of character and themes.

subject: english
question_text: His prayer to God is like a lawyer's defence of a bad case. Does he argue his case well? What are the points he makes?
answer_text: He did not argue well. He was mostly trying to impress God and make promises. He said that he had memorised the entire namaaz. He even knew the last ten suratsof the Quran by heart. He said that he was a devoted servant of God and needed the fees money. He admitted his mistake. However, in his defence, he also said that he did not eat all the jalebis. He shared them with other children. He promised that he would never eat sweets with fees money again and if he did, then he would deserve a thief's punishment. He said that there was no shortage of anything in God's treasury. Even the chaprasigot a lot of money for his work. He finally said that he was the nephew of a big officer and therefore, God should give him the money as he had asked for only four rupees.
final_answer: Therefore, his argument was weak and filled with attempts to impress rather than genuine remorse.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of character motivation and analysis of arguments.

final_answer: Thus, the game involved a playful challenge to find money hidden by God.

question_text: If God had granted his wish that day, what harm would it have caused him in later life?

final_answer: Thus, granting his wish would have hindered his moral growth.
